404 Media previously reported a vulnerability in the iCloud+ "Hide My Email" feature that allowed anyone to obtain a user's real email address. Apple now says the issue has been officially fixed.

Apple says the security flaw in "Hide My Email" was fixed earlier this month

If you're an iCloud+ or Apple One subscriber, Apple's "Hide My Email" privacy feature can be a great tool for protecting your real email address.

Below is Apple's description of how it works on its official website:

However, according to a recent report from 404 Media, "Hide My Email" has long had a vulnerability that could allow anyone to obtain the real email address linked to an Apple account. The disclosure has also triggered a newly proposed lawsuit.

Apple said today that the vulnerability was officially fixed earlier this month.

Apple told 404 Media that the company "released a fix on July 3 and said the issue has been completely resolved."

This iCloud+ vulnerability was originally reported to Apple by Tyler Murphy in June 2025. After initial communication, Apple claimed to have fixed the issue, but Murphy later discovered the problem still existed. Hopefully this time it's truly been resolved for good.

How often do you use the "Hide My Email" feature on iCloud+? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
